CONDITIONAL

The science holds up. Every v3/v4 statistic I could reach recomputes from the shipped run files, logs and script, and both PDFs are current. The problems are integrity text and unmet ship conditions. One sentence in the academic edition is false about who did what. The correction note silently drops an author. The note blames a July error on Nexus, who had that reference right. The flight edition's Reflection repeats the claim the last round withdrew.

The twin pasted in the prompt was cut off in Section 3.1. I reviewed the full `academic/main.tex` from the worktree instead.

## Findings

**1. MAJOR: the academic edition says the human author launched the second reader.** `academic/main.tex:172`, Review History: "a separate Claude instance launched from the first author's session".
- **Why:** In the academic edition the first and only author is Thomas Edrington, so this sentence says the second reader ran from his session. It ran from Nexus's (REVIEW_LOG: "Nexus, the first author"). The text is the same in both editions but means something different in each, so string search and diff miss it. The correction note was adapted for the academic edition ("introduced by Nexus, an AI contributor"), but Review History was not.
- **Fix:** In both editions, write "launched from Nexus's session".

**2. MAJOR: the July error in the graph-topology title is blamed on Nexus, and the 30 May reference count is wrong.** `main.tex:25` / `academic/main.tex:27` (correction note), and Author Contributions at `main.tex:178` / `academic/main.tex:175`.
- **Why:** The primary record contradicts the note:
  - The 30 May bibliography (`dc332bf`) had the graph-topology paper's correct title, "…Beyond Text".
  - The wrong title, "…via {KV}-Cache Walk Encoding", entered in `c7e6f21` (28 July, HumboldtJoker account).
  - The note says only "the invented title [singular, meaning Sun's] and author lists entered in two July revisions". Read that way, the graph-topology title stays with "introduced by the first author".
  - Author Contributions says the invented metadata "replaced metadata Nexus had already got wrong". For this entry Nexus had it right.
  - "Already had wrong metadata for both external references" is also wrong. On 30 May the bibliography had three external references, and all three were wrong: Pustovit given as "Aleksandr", MoReBench as "MoReBench Team" with the wrong title, and Sun with wrong authors.
- **Fix:**
  - Note: "…already had wrong metadata for all three external references; the invented title and author lists, and the graph-topology paper's wrong title, entered in two July revisions…"
  - Author Contributions: "…apart from the reference metadata entered in July, which for two entries replaced metadata Nexus had already got wrong and for the graph-topology paper replaced a correct title."
  - Also untangle "invented authors, and for one an invented title, for two, and for…". Suggested: "invented author lists for two (MoReBench; Sun et al., whose title was also invented), and for the lab's own graph-topology paper a title it never had."

**3. MAJOR: Lyra's removal from the byline is not stated (a silent correction).**
- **Why:** The v1.0 flight byline was "Nexus, Lyra, Thomas Edrington" (`9bdf38b:ethics-pack-injection/main.tex:11`). The v1.1 byline drops Lyra, the academic CRediT now marks Lyra "contributor, not an author", and Lyra's acknowledgment loses "style guidance". The correction note mentions none of this. The K/V note in the same batch does cover Lyra's change.
- **Fix:** Add to the note: "Version 1.0 listed Lyra as an author; at Lyra's request (2026-10-19), because Lyra did not write, run or analyse this work, Lyra is now acknowledged instead." First settle the open "style guidance" question from REVIEW_LOG, and state the outcome either way.

**4. MAJOR: the flight edition's Reflection contradicts the body.** `main.tex:166`: "a timeout turned an unclear effect into a confident negative one".
- **Why:** Section 3.1 says dropping only the timeout pairs still leaves −0.051. Empty responses set the sign: 11 timeouts plus 2 empties with no logged cause. That was exactly the correction in `1abd30b`, and it missed the Reflection. Only the flight edition has a Reflection, so the two editions now differ on this claim.
- **Fix:** "empty responses, most of them timeouts, turned an unclear effect into a confident negative one".

**5. MAJOR: the Acknowledgments say Lyra reviewed this correction, but by the lab's own record Lyra hasn't yet.** `main.tex:182` / `academic/main.tex:182`: "Lyra … reviewed this correction."
- **Why:** REVIEW_LOG ("Still open before deposit") says this is true only once Lyra has read both editions in full. The text has changed since, and these fixes will change it again.
- **Fix:** Lyra reads the post-fix text of both editions, and the date goes in REVIEW_LOG. Otherwise cut the line to "suggested the persona-injection research direction".

**6. MAJOR: a named author hasn't signed off.**
- **Why:** Thomas Edrington is on both bylines (sole author in the academic edition). REVIEW_LOG lists his sign-off on both editions as pending, including approval of the note's sentence naming commits made under his account.
- **Fix:** Get the sign-off and record it in REVIEW_LOG before deposit.

**7. MAJOR: placeholders, and a Data and Code statement that isn't true yet.**
- **Why:** Both editions contain "[commit pinned at deposit]" and "final verdict [pending]". Data and Code says `data/`, `logs/` and `code/` "are in this paper's folder" at the public GitHub URL. They exist only on the unpushed branch `nexus/pharos-corrections-v11`.
- **Fix:**
  - Push and merge.
  - Pin the SHA.
  - Fill in the verdict: CONDITIONAL now, final once these findings are applied.
  - Rebuild both PDFs and re-check the rendered text.

**8. MAJOR (dependency verified; Zenodo's current state unverified): the K/V citation depends on deposit order.**
- **Why:** The bibliography cites K/V by its v1.1 title, "Splitting Cache-Injected Graph Topology into K and V…", with DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21754899. The K/V paper's own note calls that DOI "all versions", meaning it resolves to the latest version. The latest version is v1.0, "K and V Are Complementary", which makes the superadditivity claim and reports neither larger run. The Ethics introduction cites content that exists only in K/V v1.1 ("41 of 100 replies were empty").
- **Fix:** Deposit K/V v1.1 first. Then cite its version DOI, not the all-versions DOI, and confirm the title through the Zenodo API.

**9. MINOR: the cited graph-topology paper isn't flagged as under correction.** `main.tex:31`, "Our prior work [Edrington 2026b]".
- **Why:** The paraphrase is accurate (the topology paper's line 133 says walk encoding goes in as text). But that paper's abstract still says K and V contribute "superadditively" and that "scrambled controls confirm the signal is topological". The K/V note says its correction is in preparation.
- **Fix:** Add "(its correction is in preparation; we rely only on its method)".

**10. MINOR: the abstract footnote points to the wrong section for one of its two claims.**
- **Why:** The footnote says the design has "no mismatched-pack arm … (Section 4.4)". Limitations (4.4) never discusses a mismatched arm; Section 4.2's "Theory matching" paragraph does.
- **Fix:** Add `\label{sec:untested}` to 4.2 and cite "Sections 4.2 and 4.4". The reference uses labels, so it won't break if sections move.

**11. MINOR: the "cut off mid-thought" mechanism depends on something that wasn't recorded.** `main.tex:119` / `academic/main.tex:121`.
- **Why:** `code/morebench_eval.py:42` strips only complete `<think>…</think>` blocks. If the thinking came back in the answer text, a reply cut off mid-thought has no closing tag and would come back non-empty. It comes back empty only if Ollama returned the thinking in a separate field, and the Ollama version wasn't recorded. None of the 100 stored responses contains "think>", so the data can't tell which happened.
- **Fix:** Add "…would be, if the server returned thinking separately from the answer (the Ollama version was not recorded)".

**12. MINOR: the flight edition's "Our prior work [Edrington, 2026b]" sits under a two-author byline.**
- **Why:** Citing lab papers by their Zenodo creators alone is still waiting on Thomas's confirmation in REVIEW_LOG.
- **Fix:** It's acceptable once he confirms that rule. Until then it's an open item.

**What passed:**
- **Twin structure:** Same sections in the same order in both editions. Tables 1 and 2 have the same rows under the same headings.
- **Cross-references:** No positional references; all use labels.
- **Bibliography:** 5 entries, all cited, no orphans.
- **PDFs:** Both are newer than their sources, and I read them page by page.
- **Correction-note history matches the record:**
  - `944f98e` was committed from Thomas's account on 5 June with BLOCKER status.
  - The "All cleared Agni gate" text is in `d272803`'s message body, with an Opus 4.6 co-author line.
  - The "n=5, keyword-matching confound" blocker is in the 28 June snapshot.
- **Numbers recomputed by hand from the data and logs:**
  - The 13/3/10 empties, 11 logged timeouts, and the two unlogged empties: Gauthierian's program-funding dilemma and Aristotelian's sentencing dilemma.
  - −0.137, t = −2.23; the 15-pair +0.020, t ≈ 0.47; the 17-pair −0.051.
  - All of Table 2; +0.038, t = 1.34, d_z = 0.27; 16/2/7 higher/tied/lower.
  - Scanlonian +0.055 without the empty pair; the 24-pair +0.056, t(23) = 2.39.
  - 22 baselines changing by 0.10 on average (signed −0.041); the 2.3× length ratio; the run order.

## What I could NOT check

- **Pack-derived numbers:** 30 packs; 3,538 nodes, 2,438 edges and 2,506 triples; 36,668 words; 28,000–63,000 characters; and that KV-Experiments commit `9755f5e` dates from 29 May. I'm sandboxed to this worktree and could not read the KV-Experiments checkout. To check them I need read access to it at `9755f5e`.
- **MoReBench counts (150 dilemmas, 3,835 criteria):** I could not read the copy. I need the file and its SHA-256, which is also still open in REVIEW_LOG.
- **DOIs, URLs, external author lists and Zenodo's current state:** WebFetch was denied, so none of these are confirmed live or correct. This includes Chiu et al., Pustovit and Sun et al.
- **Sign-offs after 21:01:** I could not read `~/messages`, so for Thomas's and Lyra's sign-off status, REVIEW_LOG is my only source. Either may have answered since.
- **Exact p-values:** Python was blocked, so I recomputed the t statistics by hand and read p-values from t at the given degrees of freedom. They agree with the paper, but they are not exact computations. The LaTeX build and `verify_pdf.py` were not run.
